The brief

A technical company that had to feel premium

The content underneath is dense by nature. Process, pillars, pricing logic. Dense is fine, but only if the page earns attention before it asks for it, so I treated the opening of every page as its own design problem: look expensive, load fast, and keep the headline perfectly readable, which is the part that usually breaks once a hero gets ambitious.

UI/UXMotion Front-EndArt Direction
How the team worked

The site is a team product, built with Agilyti's developers and copywriter. My lane is the interface and motion layer, and the code that makes it real. Everything shown on this page is work I designed and built.

Method

Designed, animated
and shipped by one person

Motion is where design handoffs quietly fail. A static frame plus a note saying "fade in" is not a spec, it is a hope. So I carry the section from the first Figma frame to the HTML the developer integrates. Here is that chain on the TalentFlow hero.

Step 01

Design the frame, then name the motion

Layout, type and colour first. Then every moving element is labelled with the behaviour it performs. FloatingCards / Levitate. PromptGlow / Breathe. PromptBar / Typing. By the time the file is done, the animation is already decided.

Step 02

Direct the imagery, do not shop for it

The landscape is generated and art directed rather than licensed. Palette, light, horizon and mood set so the background says "flow" before a word is read.

Step 03

Build it as production HTML

I write the section in HTML and CSS with easing, timing and responsive behaviour resolved. AI helps me move faster through the code, the way a plugin does, while the timing curves and every call about how it feels stay mine.

Step 04

Hand over something that already works

The developer integrates a running section instead of rebuilding a static frame. No redline round, no second pass on spacing. What ships is what was designed.

The other openings

One company,
separate worlds

The homepage above and TalentFlow are two of four openings I designed and built. Boooply is Agilyti's other product; DataJoint is a platform the team delivered. Same navigation and grid throughout, but palette, imagery and motion shift each time so no page reads as a template with the content swapped.

Boooply · AI interview platform

Evidence, not opinion.

Warm gold on near black, one portrait lit from behind, concentric rings reading as sound moving outward. Serious and human at once, which is the argument for voice screening.

DataJoint · Scientific data platform

Turn experiments into reproducible intelligence.

The deliberate inverse of Boooply. Clinical white, tight geometry, UI proof stacking in under the headline so the claim is shown, not stated.

Beyond the heroes

Sections built to hold the scroll

A hero only buys the first ten seconds. The rest of the work runs across the marketing site, the capability pages and the careers flow. These are a cross section, picked because each solved a different problem.

Service model

AI & Data Delivery Models

Three engagement models people kept confusing. Tabs hold them on one screen so they can be compared, and the orbit diagram redraws per model so the switch feels like an answer.

Client proof · Redesign

Powering ambitious teams worldwide

This one came to me already designed and not working. I kept the idea and rebuilt the execution: blurred photographic backgrounds so each card carries its own world, recorded product footage inside them, and a horizontal drag so the proof reads as a reel instead of a grid.

Capability deep dive

Every layer of the MLOps stack

The most technical content on the site. Four pipeline stages, each with its own diagram, held in one panel so the reader controls the depth instead of facing a wall of spec.

Proof

Proven operational impact

The three numbers the company is built on. Each card carries a small chart that draws itself in, so the figure arrives with evidence attached.

Careers

Always hiring

A job list is usually the deadest page a company has. Roles cycle in oversized type while a node diagram rebuilds for whichever one is active, so the list reads as a living team.

Careers · Apply flow

Role detail and application

Straight UX rather than presentation. Role detail on the left, a single-screen application on the right, short enough that finishing never feels like a task.

Insights · Art direction

Our blog, insights, articles, news

My favourite. Every image directed and composed as one set, so the strip reads as a single body of work instead of stock picked article by article.

Directed, not sourced. One palette, one light source, one recurring silhouette, with the wolf mark surfacing inside the artwork. That is why the carousel can move fast without the eye losing the thread.
